findings: The complete November 2026 capture retains the title and regional-limitation description and lists iOS, Android and React Native variant links without their bodies (new raw 1–15; old raw 4–12, 335–340 and 630–635). The old capture was fetched 2026-04-23 despite the filename. Diff line 931 joins the old ending and first new link, and the actual snapshots give the boundary (old raw 926–930; new raw 13–15).

The 2026-04-23 restricted integration is for businesses accepting only US and Canadian cards. Client card fields collect sensitive details and `createPaymentMethod` supplies an ID to the merchant server. The server decides the amount and creates/confirms a PaymentIntent with `confirm: true` and `error_on_requires_action: true`. The immediate server result supports post-payment actions when `succeeded`; an authentication request causes an error rather than customer authentication (old raw 12–34, 112–178, 180–265, 290–316, 414–473 and 715–775).

The existing source correctly retains the basic approach and three separate platform UI components. Its use criterion weakens the old card scope, its webhook language omits the restriction to immediate actions in the synchronous server flow, and its response prose obscures non-authentication card declines and unexpected server outcomes. A correct retrieval answer also needs the explicit server-owned amount and the distinction between creating the client PaymentMethod and server payment success (source 13–34, 38–58; old raw 12–34, 162–178, 191–196 and 216–325).

The existing acceptance source’s all-`Failed` upgrade shorthand at line 70 loses the authentication scope of the related migration guidance. The April mobile acceptance example and the April mobile and November Payment Intents migration documents use distinct response fields/diagnostics. The reciprocal in-app routes at concept lines 113 and 115 should use the documented “basic” wording or explicitly mark “Legacy” as editorial. The pinned documents provide no formal deprecation statement.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the 2026-04-23 scope to businesses accepting only US and Canadian cards and preserve the tradeoff that an issuer request for authentication causes a decline instead of an authentication flow. The April guide routes growing/global businesses and authentication-required payments toward Stripe’s authentication-capable integration (old raw 12–34 and 329–333, repeated for Android and React Native).

Keep the dated iOS `STPPaymentCardTextField` in `StripePaymentsUI`, Android `CardInputWidget`, and React Native `CardField`, with client-side card collection and PaymentMethod creation followed by passing its ID to a trusted server. The examples use publishable client configuration and distinguish test keys from live keys. Android 23.5.0 and iOS 13 are historic sample claims. The Financial Connections dependency comment concerns US bank accounts, while this payment guide describes cards (old raw 38–48, 93–114, 162–195, 369–414, 454–490, 682–719 and 754–792).

Preserve the server-authoritative amount and immediate confirm attempt. The sample uses `succeeded` to gate immediate fulfillment and treats other returned statuses as unexpected. The authentication failure example shows `authentication_required`, `authentication_not_handled` and `requires_payment_method`; the insufficient-funds and successful cards are separate test scenarios (old raw 191–265 and 290–327).

The archived explanation permits immediate post-payment actions from the synchronous server result in this restricted path. The comparison table recommends webhooks in the global integration (old raw 18–34). PaymentMethod creation, a success-path API example, and sandbox test outcomes do not establish live payment, settlement, broad eligibility, or current SDK support.

Source lines 13, 48 and 57 and reciprocal in-app concept line 113 compress the restricted synchronous example into a general no-webhook claim. Old raw 18–34 and 245–255 scope that to immediate post-payment actions from the server’s `succeeded` branch, and the global route recommends webhooks.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-mobile-without-card-authentication-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-inapp-without-card-auth-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-without-card-auth.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/without-card-authentication`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/without-card-authentication, new raw lines 5-15 describe a simpler region-limited integration and route to iOS, Android and React Native. The April 23, 2026 capture supplies the actual behavior. Old raw lines 12-34 scope it to businesses accepting only US and Canadian cards and say an issuer authentication request immediately fails the payment. The dated client components are iOS `STPPaymentCardTextField` in `StripePaymentsUI`, Android `CardInputWidget` and React Native `CardField` (old raw lines 112-123, 412-415 and 715-722). Client-side creation of a PaymentMethod supplies its ID to the server (old raw lines 162-178, 454-473 and 754-775). The server chooses the amount and creates and confirms a PaymentIntent with `confirm: true` and `error_on_requires_action: true`. The sample gates immediate fulfillment on server-observed `succeeded`, while the authentication-error example uses `authentication_required`, `authentication_not_handled` and `requires_payment_method` (old raw lines 191-265 and 290-316). source-stripe-inapp-without-card-auth.md captures the core path but needs to correct its looser regional use criterion and scope its no-webhook and error wording to the documented example.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/without-card-authentication, new raw lines 5-15 add only navigation to the platform variants represented in old raw lines 8-12, 335-340 and 630-635. The pinned evidence shows no substantive product change. Date the April 23, 2026 scope to businesses accepting only US and Canadian cards and distinguish the client PaymentMethod from the server-created and immediately confirmed PaymentIntent. The April example applies its no-webhook shortcut only to immediate post-payment actions from the trusted server response, with fulfillment gated on `succeeded`. The global route handles authentication requests and recommends webhooks (old raw lines 12-34 and 193-265). In source-stripe-inapp-without-card-auth.md and the reciprocal in-app route, qualify the regional criterion and no-webhook wording, keep issuer-authentication errors separate from insufficient-funds and other errors, and retain the April client UI names: iOS `STPPaymentCardTextField` in `StripePaymentsUI`, Android `CardInputWidget` and React Native `CardField` (old raw lines 112-123, 412-415 and 715-722). Use the guide’s “basic” wording for this dated integration. In the April 23, 2026 acceptance sample, `error.code=authentication_required` pairs with `decline_code=authentication_not_handled` and PaymentIntent `requires_payment_method`; insufficient funds is a separate sandbox scenario (old raw lines 290-327). Scope the line 70 upgrade wording and reciprocal mobile migration route to many failures like the authentication-required Dashboard example or the API diagnostic `requires_action_not_handled`. That distinct diagnostic appears in the April 23 mobile migration capture (raw/stripe-inapp-upgrade-to-handle-actions-2025.md:4-17) and the separate November 7 Payment Intents migration capture (raw/stripe-payments-payment-intents-upgrade-to-handle-actions-2026-11-07.md:5-14). Neither diagnostic is a novel finding from the November acceptance selector, and an ordinary card decline does not establish the migration condition. A test response or the new index cannot verify current compatibility, merchant eligibility, live payment success or settlement.
